mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the last three months signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are negatively impacted.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances when RSAFS declines for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the last month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO increases by more than 1% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% within the last month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances when UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (change within ±0.5%) over the last month, it signals a positive demand shock without inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% and CPIAUCSL changes within ±0.5%
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances when HOUST increases by more than 5% and CPIAUCSL changes within ±0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS is above 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% within the last month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances when PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2%.
